## Scope

The initial [lecture audit](yqx-panel-lectures.qmd) identified a
confirmed standalone synthetic-control optimization defect, different
fixed-effect inference conventions, and missing causal-panel interfaces.
This implementation addresses the solver defect and adds the core FE prediction,
imputation, and covariance interfaces. It does **not** implement the entire
new-estimator roadmap.

[FE imputation documentation](../examples/fe-imputation.qmd) ·
[Fixed-effects regression documentation](../examples/fixed-effects-ols.qmd) ·
[Synthetic control documentation](../examples/synthetic-control.qmd) ·
[Updated development specification](https://github.com/apoorvalal/crabbymetrics/blob/v0.9.1/replications/yqx_panel/SPEC.md)

## Synthetic control

The standalone estimator now solves the squared-error objective directly on the
simplex with an active-set quadratic solver. Zero donor weights are permitted.
The old softmax parameterization could yield nearly flat gradients at a
suboptimal solution. Returning a finite parameter vector no longer suffices:
convergence requires a KKT optimality check, and exhausted iteration budgets
raise an error.

For Proposition 99 outcome-only SCM:

| Quantity | Before | Corrected | Independent reference |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Pre-treatment RMSE | 2.399913 | 1.656400 | 1.656400 |
| Mean post-treatment gap | −18.998496 | −19.513630 | −19.513630 |

The corrected solve takes 34 active-set iterations in the recorded run.
`summary()` exposes the objective, iterations, feasibility error, normalized KKT
residual and stopping reason. Tests check boundary optima, redundant donors,
donor permutations, common-level shifts, single-donor inputs, failed-refit state,
and insufficient iteration budgets. This is outcome-only SCM, not predictor-V SCM.

## Fixed-effect regression

`FixedEffectsOLS` now exposes absorption tolerance and iteration limits, supports
FE-only fits, compacts caller-supplied FE IDs, retains level effects, and predicts
identified one/two-way FE sums. Unseen levels and combinations crossing
disconnected components are rejected. Three-or-more-way level prediction remains
unsupported, while slope estimation still supports it.

The default full-FE degrees-of-freedom correction is preserved. New explicit
options control FE counting, observation-count correction and cluster-count
correction in both summaries and Wald tests. The fatalities example verifies:

| Convention | Explicit settings beyond cluster IDs | SE |
|---|---|---:|
| Existing CrabbyMetrics default | defaults | 0.385787 |
| fixest lecture default | `fe_df="non_nested"` | 0.357078 |
| plm HC1 lecture calculation | `fe_df="none", ssc="hc1", cluster_correction=False` | 0.350150 |

All three retain the coefficient −0.639980. These are deliberate statistical
conventions, not three competing numerical answers to one covariance formula.

## Native FE counterfactuals

`FEImputation` uses the same sparse absorption machinery. It fits
$Y_{it}(0)=\alpha_i+\lambda_t+X_{it}'\beta$ only on observed positive-weight
untreated cells. It accepts missing observations and treatment reversals,
returns exact training/evaluation masks, and aggregates weighted observed-treated
cell gaps by unit and time. It rejects unsupported FE combinations and nuisance
covariates unidentified in the untreated sample.

The five available empirical surfaces are compared with the already-saved R
FEct outputs below. No treated outcome enters estimation. This is point
estimation, **without confidence intervals or causal validation of treatment
reversals**.

```{python}
from pathlib import Path
import os
import json
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import crabbymetrics as cm

root = Path(os.environ['YQX_REPLICATION_ROOT']) if 'YQX_REPLICATION_ROOT' in os.environ else next(
    p / 'replications/yqx_panel' for p in [Path.cwd(), *Path.cwd().parents]
    if (p / 'replications/yqx_panel/results/fixes').exists())
verification = json.loads((root / 'results/fixes/verification.json').read_text())
panel_results = pd.read_csv(root / 'results/fixes/panels.csv')
display(panel_results.loc[panel_results.model != 'prop99_scm',
    ['model', 'att', 'reference_att', 'max_surface_error', 'n_train', 'n_treated']])
```

Bischof's surface agreement uses a $10^{-6}$ tolerance because its saved R fit
has looser convergence. The other examples agree much more closely. These
comparisons do not erase the initial audit's sample/provenance differences.

## Executable leakage and support check

```{python}
rng = np.random.default_rng(210921)
x = rng.normal(size=(12, 8, 1))
y = rng.normal(size=(12, 1)) + np.arange(8)[None, :] / 4 + .5*x[:, :, 0]
d = np.zeros_like(y)
d[6:, 4:6] = 1  # treatment can subsequently switch off
observed = np.ones_like(d, dtype=bool)
observed[0, 0] = False
y += 2*d
m = cm.FEImputation()
m.fit(y, d, x, observed=observed)
original = m.predict()
print('ATT:', m.summary()['att'])
y[d == 1] += 100
m.fit(y, d, x, observed=observed)
np.testing.assert_allclose(m.predict(), original, equal_nan=True, atol=1e-10)
assert abs(m.summary()['att'] - 102) < 1e-8
print('No treated-outcome leakage; shifted ATT:', m.summary()['att'])
```

## Regression protection and reproducibility

```{python}
assert verification['linear']['specifications'] == 59
assert verification['linear']['coefficients'] == 102
assert verification['linear']['max_coef_error'] < 1e-8
assert verification['archive']['datasets'] == 47
assert verification['archive']['max_coef_error'] < 1e-8
print('Lecture regressions:', verification['linear'])
print('Archive regressions:', verification['archive'])
```

- Standard tests use original deterministic fixtures generated independently in
  base R. `lm` supplies coefficient/counterfactual references; full-design cluster
  score calculations supply covariance references; exhaustive simplex-face
  optimization supplies an independent small SCM optimum. The generation script
  is checked in; routine tests do not require R or a network connection.
- Optional empirical tests replay Proposition 99, the five FEct examples, and
  the three fatalities covariance conventions using the ignored acquired data.
  They skip when the cache is unavailable rather than downloading data during CI.
- `replications/yqx_panel/verify_fixes.py` reruns 59 lecture specifications and
  47 archive regressions, plus SCM and imputation checks, against frozen R
  outputs. Post-fix results live in `results/fixes/`; original audit outputs are
  preserved. Schäfer uses the tightly converged R reference established by the
  initial audit.
- Tests compare the appropriate reference specifications. Forty-seven archive
  regressions do not mean 47 complete replications of every estimator/inference
  pipeline. Two are explicitly baseline-only, and the two huge datasets remain
  outside the current memory budget.

## Recorded implementation validation

The September 21 implementation run recorded **343 passing tests and one intermittent failure**
in the existing benchmark process-group cleanup test (`os.killpg` raises a macOS
permission error after the parent exits). Both cleanup cases pass when rerun in
isolation. All 24 new tests pass. No skip or change to that process runner was
made, and the full suite is not labeled green. Details are in
[test-status.json](https://github.com/apoorvalal/crabbymetrics/blob/v0.9.1/replications/yqx_panel/results/fixes/test-status.json).

The current release has separate [CI and package artifacts](https://github.com/apoorvalal/crabbymetrics/releases/tag/v0.9.1). The historical local result above is preserved rather than presented as a current CI failure.

## Remaining work

The implementation does not add causal IFEct/MCct, Sun–Abraham or group-time DID,
varying-slope absorption, multiway clustering, joint event-study inference,
bootstrap imputation inference, augmented/predictor-V SCM, or factorial-DID
nuisance orchestration. They remain explicitly proposed in the specification.
The existing absorbing-only estimators have not been silently broadened to
missing or reversing treatment panels. These implementations were merged in PR #23 and are included in v0.9.1.
